acceptanceCriteria: The failure detail of TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts under a full `go test ./cmd/corvint` run is captured and classified (deadline, process spawn, or assertion).
If it is a load-sensitive deadline, the test either uses a hang-detector bound per decision 0082 or reports the bound it hit; it passes reliably in a full-package run on a loaded host.
It still passes when run alone.
body: Suspected, not yet reproduced on demand. Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, clone of branch claude/502-escalations-record-key (cmd/corvint unchanged by the branch, which touches internal/taskman and internal/tasks only), TMPDIR=/private/tmp/c502t. `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/taskman ./internal/tasks/{ticket,mutation,importer,transaction,wire} ./cmd/corvint` (other heavy go test runs on the same host at the time) failed `--- FAIL: TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts (60.82s)`; the package took 1497 s. The failure body was not captured because the output was filtered to summary lines. Rerunning `-run 'TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts$' ./cmd/corvint` alone passed (72.9 s). Expected: no failure under host load. Inference: the 60.82 s duration suggests a one-minute bound (cmd/corvint/host_adapter_test.go uses time.Minute dogfood-event deadlines and hang detectors) reached under load; this is unconfirmed.
title: Suspected flake: TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts fails at ~60 s in a loaded full cmd/corvint run, passes alone
